title: The Flexible arrangement for the work
subtitle: 服务职业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）
meta: 主题语境：服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）　|　核心词汇：flexible　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 flexible 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 the painter wrote of ① a flexible arrangement for the work in the catalogue, and everybody in the studio said at once that it was ② more flexible than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the painter, who never explained anything, had done it twice over and gone home; it was the flexible ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most flexible arrangement for the work anybody in the studio had ever seen, or so the catalogue for May 1949 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too flexible to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the visitor who had come to help; the flexible ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the brush at the far easel, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a flexible rule about the hours, and said that no visitor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as flexible as the rule about the hours they had once had in the old studio. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was flexible or not, and he said so.

By 1962 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the catalogue. What the line asked for was ⑦ something flexible, and nothing besides. The visitor from the next studio called the whole plan ⑧ quite flexible; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the catalogue kept the names of the flexible ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1965, year after year, she wrote of another flexible arrangement for the work in the same catalogue, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ more flexible than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most flexible rule about the hours in the whole studio, she said in 1967, was the one she could never quite name; the flexible ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 灵活（前置定语 a flexible arrangement for the work：1955 年画师在展品目录里记下的那件灵活的安排）
B. adj. 灵活／可变通（比较级 more flexible than：文中两处，一处比工作上的灵活安排，一处比预想）
C. adj. 灵活／可变通（最高级 the most flexible：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 灵活（表语 too flexible to do：母亲觉得它太灵活，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 可变通（前置定语 a flexible rule about the hours：叔叔把整件事称作一桩可变通的变通规矩）
F. adj. 可变通（同级比较 as flexible as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩工时的变通规矩相比）
G. adj. 可变通（后置定语 something flexible：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 可变通（受程度副词修饰 quite flexible：那位观者的评价）

items.q: a flexible arrangement for the work
the most flexible arrangement for the work anybody
a flexible rule about the hours
The most flexible rule about the hours in

answers.why: flexible 意为“灵活”，1955 年画师在展品目录里记下的是“一件灵活的安排”，此处作前置定语 a flexible arrangement for the work。
flexible 意为“灵活”，此处用比较级 more flexible than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
flexible 意为“灵活”，展品目录上 五月 那行字说它是画室里最灵活的一件，故用最高级 the most flexible arrangement for the work。
flexible 意为“灵活”，母亲认为这件东西“太灵活了，谁也用不上”，too flexible to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
flexible 意为“可变通”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩可变通的变通规矩”，此处作前置定语 a flexible rule about the hours。
flexible 意为“可变通”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩工时的变通规矩一样可变通”，同级比较用 as flexible as。
flexible 意为“可变通”，展品目录上那半行字要的是“可变通的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something flexible。
flexible 意为“可变通”，邻画室来的那位观者认为这套计划“相当可变通”，quite 修饰原级 flexible。
flexible 意为“可变通”，1965 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要可变通”，故用比较级 more flexible than。
flexible 意为“可变通”，母亲 1967 年说的是“整个画室里最可变通的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most flexible rule about the hours。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1955 年，画师在展品目录里记下了一件灵活的安排。（a flexible arrangement for the work）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更灵活。（more flexible than …）
母亲觉得它太灵活，谁也用不上。（too flexible to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩可变通的变通规矩。（a flexible rule about the hours）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩工时的变通规矩一样可变通。（as flexible as …）
到了 1962 年，展品目录上只剩半行字：要的是一件可变通的东西。（something flexible）
answers: In 1955 the painter wrote of a flexible arrangement for the work in the catalogue.
Everybody said it was more flexible than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too flexible to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a flexible rule about the hours.
He said nobody would call it as flexible as the rule about the hours they had once had.
By 1962 the catalogue asked for nothing but something flexible.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 flexible 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1955 the painter wrote of a flexible arrangement for the work in the catalogue, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most flexible arrangement for the work in the studio, or so the catalogue says.
My mother thought it too flexible to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a flexible rule about the hours, and nobody argued with him.
The visitor from the next studio called the plan quite flexible, and everybody laughed.
The flexible ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
